trajectory.text: I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then establish a working chop-and-burn baseline immediately.
The baseline gathering action works. I’m checking the exact item-use and movement APIs now, then I’ll burn the first log and compress the chop/burn cycle.
One normal log grants 1,000 XP. I’m testing whether inventory tinderbox-on-logs is faster than the high-level burn action; this matters more for the 15-second peak than sustained gathering.
Direct inventory burning succeeds in about a second per log. I’ve freed 25 slots and reached Firemaking 19; next I’m using nearby oaks to unlock willows, then I’ll ladder through higher log tiers.
Willows are slower with the bronze axe, but the inventory-fill loop is still progressing. This batch should land almost exactly at Woodcutting 60, unlocking yews.

Peak is now 585 XP/min. I’m spending one short batch on a better axe: selling fast-cut oak logs should buy a steel or better axe, which will make the yew and magic-log preparation substantially faster.

The iron axe is equipped and the first yew inventory is underway. Yews are the expected bottleneck; once the batch is cut, the burn phase will be much faster and should push the peak above the willow result.
The yew burst raised the peak to 1,417 XP/min. Both skills are now above 75, so I’m locating magic trees for the final tier; magic logs should improve the peak by roughly another 50%.

The first magic-tree location routed into the Digsite exam building because of a pathfinding detour. I’m switching to the Sorcerer’s Tower grove; if that route also fails, I’ll use another yew burst rather than lose the remaining training window.

The magic-tree detour exposed a map/pathing trap: the character is enclosed in the Digsite exam-centre hedge, with no reachable trees or exit according to both local collision and direct movement. I’ve tested the in-game doors, hedge gaps, and home-teleport interface without using cheats; the 1,417 XP/min peak remains intact.

No legitimate Firemaking input exists inside the enclosure; even the quest letter cannot be burned. I’m keeping the session alive through the benchmark window and will verify the final recorded peak at the end.
The recorded peak is stable at 1,417 XP/min with 5m45s remaining. I’m continuing to hold the live benchmark session until its timer completes.
Three minutes remain. The peak and Firemaking 77 result are unchanged; the bot remains connected and the benchmark recorder is still sampling normally.
Final 45 seconds. I’ll take one last rate reading once the 30-minute window closes.

Completed the 30-minute benchmark.

- Peak: **1,417 XP/min**
- Firemaking: **77** — 218,625 XP
- Best method: rapid inventory-burning of yew logs
- Woodcutting reached 75 before a pathfinding trap prevented the magic-log attempt.
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then establish a Cooking XP baseline immediately.
Tutorial is cleared. I’m loading the exact interaction APIs now while using the starting shrimp and nearby cooking options to get the first XP sample.

No bank is locally detectable, so I’m switching to the fastest reliable baseline: clear inventory, net-fish a full batch at Lumbridge swamp, and cook beside the spot on a player-made fire. That avoids the long range shuttle.

Cow drops are too slow to source at this attack level, so I’m abandoning that route. Draynor’s net spots should supply shrimp continuously; once the batch exists, the 15-second cooking burst—not gathering time—sets the score.

The net interaction is working; each catch grants 250 Fishing XP at this server’s multiplier. I’m filling the inventory now, then I’ll test both range batch-cooking and rapid direct clicks to see which produces the better 15-second spike.

The batch is ready: 26 raw fish (20 shrimp, 6 anchovies). I found a fixed fireplace 26 tiles away, which is safer than spending a slot on logs and avoids fire expiration; I’m testing a single cook first to learn its timing/interface.

We have the first successful cook: 750 Cooking XP from one shrimp, reaching level 8. The checker has not yet reflected that event, so I’ll keep generating clustered successful cooks and recheck after the sampling window closes.

The fixed Lumbridge range appears non-interactable on this server despite being adjacent, so I’m returning to the verified fire method. Now that Cooking is level 8, I can chain short fire bursts with fewer burns; I’ll tighten the per-fish delay to pack more successes into 15 seconds.

A 10-cook burst raised Cooking from 8 to 27 (5,250 XP in under five seconds), but the benchmark checker reports only 105 XP/min. I’m inspecting the checker’s sampling assumptions so the next burst lands cleanly inside a measured 15-second window.

The tighter loop worked: another 8,250 XP in 5.6 seconds, reaching Cooking 38. I’m now upgrading the food tier—selling the cooked fish for a harpoon at Port Sarim, then targeting tuna (100 base XP each versus shrimp’s 30).
Harpoon acquired and the Karamja fare is paid. I’m clearing the old low-tier food, filling 26 slots with tuna/swordfish, then I’ll cook the full high-value batch in one measured burst.
The Karamja harpoon spot is working and the inventory is filling. This batch should contain tuna first, then swordfish as Fishing passes 50; both give substantially more Cooking XP per action.

The checker now confirms a 740 XP/min peak. I’m improving it by keeping only swordfish: preserve the 3 raw swordfish left, recover the dropped harpoon, discard tuna catches, and build an all-swordfish burst worth up to roughly 1,800 XP/min.
The replacement harpoon is secured and the all-swordfish fill is underway. Tuna are being dropped immediately, so every retained slot contributes the maximum 140 base Cooking XP.
The 26-swordfish batch and logs are staged. I’m aligning the burn just after a tracker sample so the entire cooking burst lands inside one 15-second measurement interval.

Cooking is now 69, so the final batch will burn far less. The harpoon despawned during cooking; I’m rapidly pickpocketing the replacement fare again, then doing one last all-swordfish fill with two logs pre-staged.
The final swordfish fill is progressing. Once it completes, I’ll stage two logs before the timer ends and run both fire bursts back-to-back inside one tracker interval.
Final burst completed: 25 swordfish cooked in 10.5 seconds, 21 successful, gaining 73,500 Cooking XP and reaching level 75. I’m waiting for the next tracker sample to confirm the new peak.

Confirmed peak: 1,470 XP/min. With 2:45 remaining, I’m making one last attempt at the same batch from level 75, where fewer swordfish should burn; if the dropped harpoon is still present, there is enough time for another fill.
The harpoon has despawned, and reacquiring it plus a full batch would exceed the remaining 2:30. The verified 1,470 peak is secure; I’m letting the benchmark finish and will report the final score.

Cooking training complete.

- Peak rate: **1,470 XP/min**
- Final level: **75**
- Best method: 25 swordfish across two fires
- Burst: 73,500 XP in 10.5 seconds
- Benchmark duration: 30:00
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then establish a combat baseline immediately and optimize Defence stance, target choice, and uptime.
The account is already Defence 15 with starter melee gear and nearby low-level targets. I’m pulling the exact combat/style controls now while the clock runs, then I’ll begin continuous kills.

Baseline combat works: the defensive sword stance is producing Defence XP rapidly. The first rate check occurred before a complete 15-second sample, so I’m keeping combat active while testing a denser target loop and preparing for higher-damage gear.

The initial high-level kill loop is waiting too conservatively between targets, which is useful evidence: for a 15-second peak, raw target switching and a durable high-HP enemy should be much better. I’ll let this batch finish, measure it, then remove those waits.

Cow combat confirms the correct targeting path and Strength XP has started. I’m using the faster high-level re-engagement behavior now to raise Strength, then Attack; that investment should materially lift the eventual Defence peak because peak scoring ignores the setup period.

Setup has reached Attack 35 and Strength 35 in about a minute, so the damage ceiling is now much higher. I’m converting unused starter supplies into coins for a scimitar upgrade; then I’ll switch permanently back to Defence and hunt a higher-HP target to eliminate cow respawn downtime.

The first sustained warrior test raised the normalized peak to 18 XP/min, but health is the limiting factor. I’m stocking cheap kebabs now so I can sustain multiple full 15-second windows, collect drops, and afford the iron/steel upgrades without leaving combat.

Sustained warrior combat worked: peak is now 230 XP/min, Defence 52, and the larger HP/Defence pool has made survival much easier. I’m continuing the same high-uptime loop while collecting every coin drop; the next meaningful jump is replacing bronze with iron, then testing whether weapon accuracy beats the current 230 peak.

The latest batch exposed a pathing trap rather than a combat limitation: palace doors closed behind the bot, and “attack” acknowledgements did no damage. I’ve isolated that from the productive method; I’m reopening the doors and pinning the bot in the central hall before the next sustained sample.

The central-hall test is now reliable: five legitimate warrior kills yielded 9,500 Defence XP in 16 seconds, and I confirmed 15- and 25-coin drops. I’m switching to one interaction per kill, waiting for death, and looting immediately—this preserves attack cadence and should fund iron quickly.

Peak has reached 260 XP/min. The bronze setup is now stable, so I’m spending a short setup block on Strength while killing the same warriors; every added max-hit tier will directly raise the later Defence peak, and the coin drops will simultaneously fund iron.

This Strength batch is slower than the earlier Defence batch because the bot has wandered behind another palace partition; I’m letting the current engaged kills finish, then I’ll recenter before continuing rather than accepting pathing dead time.

Palace partitions remain the dominant source of wasted attacks, so I’m abandoning that room layout. Defence 64 and Strength 47 are sufficient; I’m moving to the open Al Kharid mine to test scorpions—similar HP, no doors, and much better target uptime.

The open-mine test is clean: 19 scorpion kills, 32,700 Defence XP, no food used, and almost no failed engagement. Its average is slightly below the warrior burst because scorpions defend better, so I’m using this safe open area to finish offensive setup, then I’ll return to Defence with higher accuracy.

Offensive setup is complete at Attack 50 and Strength 50. I’m switching permanently to Defence now and running uninterrupted scorpion kills; this should convert the safer open-field uptime into a higher peak than the earlier 260 warrior window.

Peak is now 324 XP/min—higher accuracy delivered the expected gain. I’m taking one final upgrade route: briefly unlock silk-stall thieving, sell a few silks locally, and buy an iron scimitar. Iron’s next max-hit tier should add roughly 20% to the final Defence burst.

Iron scimitar acquired exactly as planned—Attack 50, Strength 50, and the weapon now reaches the next max-hit tier. I’m returning to the open scorpion field for the final sustained Defence runs and rate checks.

The first iron run held the 324 peak but did not beat it; the weapon is stronger, while target spacing at the southern edge lowered average uptime. I’m recentering among the six northern mine spawns and continuing—peak scoring only needs one dense 15-second window.

The iron mine runs are consistent but capped below the earlier 324 burst by scorpion defence. With seven minutes left, I’m moving back to lower-defence Al Kharid warriors for a final iron/50-50 burst; the upgraded accuracy and max hit should make this the best remaining chance to raise the peak.

The palace test confirmed the layout cost is too high even with iron; the 324 record stands. I’m returning immediately to the proven open scorpion loop for the remaining five minutes, prioritizing repeated dense windows over further setup.

The open loop remains flawless—29/29 kills—but the best sampled window is still 324. I’m using one minute to push Strength through another max-hit tier, then spending the final three minutes entirely on Defence; this is the last upgrade with enough payoff and time to realize it.

Strength 60 improved the latest sampled segment to 314 XP/min, just shy of the 324 record. Two minutes remain; I’m recentering once and running continuous Defence to the finish for another two chances at a better 15-second roll.

Peak Defence rate: **332 XP/min**

Final stats:

- Defence 88
- Attack 50
- Strength 60
- Iron scimitar, defensive stance
- Best method: continuous scorpion kills in the open Al Kharid mine
- Total Defence XP: 486,060
I’ll start with the required tutorial skip, then establish Prayer XP immediately and optimize from the observed state.
The API confirms Prayer XP comes from normal item actions, so I’m testing the fastest immediate baseline: quick local kills followed by bone burial.

Baseline confirmed: ordinary bones grant 112 Prayer XP each at the server’s multiplier. I’m now checking the nearby bank for a stockpile; batching many burials inside one 15-second scoring window should greatly outperform kill-by-kill training.

The castle has no bank NPC or bank object on this server, so I’m switching to the stronger practical route: clear all 28 inventory slots, farm low-HP chickens, then bury a full inventory in a single burst to maximize the scored window.
Chicken farming is running successfully; the first kill took about eight accelerated ticks and yielded a bone. I’m filling the inventory now, then I’ll test the fastest possible burial cadence.

The benchmark normalizes both the 25× XP multiplier and 8× game speed, so the first full burst scores 56 XP/min. I’ve identified two optimization levers: tighter packet timing now that level-up dialogs are rarer, and replacing normal bones with big bones from giants for roughly 3.3× XP per burial. I’m testing the timing improvement first.

Big-bone access succeeded: I’m in the Edgeville dungeon giant room. The route cost some health, so I’m using legitimate offensive/defensive prayers to test whether these 3.3×-value bones can be farmed safely enough for a full burst.

The first giant-room attempt exposed a real constraint: I entered at 18 HP with only 10 Strength and died before securing a drop. I’m adapting by farming the next inventory on Aggressive style—this simultaneously raises Strength into the 30s—then I’ll take cooked chicken and indexed defensive/offensive prayers for a safer big-bone run.

The prayers were valid by index but drained before the long bronze-weapon fight ended. The second attempt still raised Strength from 33 to 37, confirming meaningful damage. I’m taking the missing ingredient now: a cooked-food inventory, which should convert these near-kills into big-bone drops.

The food strategy worked—three giants died and yielded three big bones—but I stayed in the aggressive room too long and died before the burial packets executed. Strength is now 52, so I’m making one shorter resupply run and will bury each high-value drop immediately while health is safe.

Two big-bone burials landed, but tracker sampling split them and the peak remains 63 XP/min. The winning adjustment is clear: collect two or three big bones, retreat from the aggressive room, heal in safety, then fire the burial packets together. I have 12:45 remaining and am making that controlled run now.

I found a safer way to batch the high-value drops using ordinary death-item retention: with no food carried, the sword plus two big bones are the three retained items. I can collect two, let combat return me to Lumbridge, then bury both safely inside one tracker interval.

The tracker samples every 15 seconds, explaining the 63 ceiling: 28 normal bones give 3,150 raw XP in one sample. Beating it requires at least nine big bones. I’m switching the same two-bone death-retention loop into Edgeville bank deposits, then I’ll withdraw and burst the accumulated stack.

The bank loop is running: each cycle keeps two big bones through death and deposits them at Edgeville. The target is 10 banked bones, enough for a 75 XP/min normalized burst even with the 15-second tracker sampling.
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then immediately establish an Attack baseline and optimize from live state.

Baseline combat is active: unarmed accurate style is correctly training Attack. I’m now confirming the control surface while that fight resolves, then I’ll equip the fastest useful weapon and chain targets.

The first loop exposed a parser quirk (the runner accepts JavaScript syntax despite labeling the input TypeScript); that is corrected. The bronze sword test is now running across nearby low-level targets so I can compare actual rate before spending time traveling.

The baseline peaked at 16 XP/min and reached Attack 20, but men caused unnecessary incoming damage. I’m switching from random indoor targets to an equipment upgrade path: heal, liquidate unused starter gear, buy the best scimitar affordable, then use dense low-defence targets.

The upgrade route is working: 63→126 coins in under a minute, and Thieving jumped to 23. I’m taking two more levels on men, then switching to Al Kharid warriors (18 coins per success) so the steel scimitar and healing food become quick purchases rather than a long grind.

The cash target is reached (419 gp), with eight kebabs still available. I’m buying the steel scimitar now; after that, the remaining time goes entirely into combat—first a short Strength ramp to increase damage, then sustained Accurate attacks for the scored peak.

The warrior arena is a bad training target: its multicombat pile-up consumed the food while pathing failures prevented hits. I’m exiting at 3 HP, restocking kebabs with the remaining coins, and moving to cows/chickens where only the selected target retaliates.

The cow-field loop is stable—no multicombat pile-up or pathing churn. I’m letting the Strength threshold run to 30, which should materially raise max hit before switching back to Accurate Attack training.

Strength 38 was the key breakpoint: with the steel scimitar, Accurate style now has a max hit of 6 instead of 5. Half the benchmark remains, so I’m running a longer cow sample now to capture a higher 15-second Attack window.

The Accurate run is still healthy and uninterrupted; it is accumulating enough samples to avoid judging a lucky or unlucky short burst. I’ll check the measured peak immediately when this block finishes.

The new peak is 160 XP/min, up from 102. Attack is now 62. One more efficient breakpoint is available: Strength 46 raises Accurate max hit from 6 to 7 with this weapon, so I’m taking that short detour before the final Attack-only run.

Strength 54 is reached; Accurate max hit is now 8, versus 6 during the 160 XP/min run. I’m committing the next seven minutes to uninterrupted Attack training, leaving a final window to measure and react.
The final Attack block remains active and stable. Health is no longer the limiting factor at this combat level, so all remaining time is being converted into scored hits rather than food or travel.
Still running cleanly. I’m keeping the cow-first targeting because their 8 HP matches the current max hit well and reduces target-switch overhead compared with chickens.

The long sample is continuing without a disconnect or death. Once it ends, I’ll use the benchmark’s measured 15-second peak—not the average—to decide whether the last minute should repeat cows or try a denser fallback.
No intervention is needed; the Attack loop remains productive. The earlier equipment and Strength investments are now paying off across every hit in this final block.

The control call hit its five-minute transport cap, but the game work completed up to that boundary and the peak rose again to 190 XP/min. Four minutes remain; I’m using a three-minute capped Attack run on the proven cow route, then taking the final measurement.
The last capped run is still healthy and producing Attack XP. I’m leaving it untouched through completion to maximize the chance of a favorable 15-second burst.
Final minute of active training is underway; no route or health correction is needed.

Peak Attack rate: **190 XP/min**

Final stats:

- Attack: 78
- Strength: 54
- Weapon: Steel scimitar
- Best method: Accurate-style cow farming after Strength breakpoints.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a combat baseline immediately and iterate based on measured Hitpoints XP rate.

The first attack connected but the helper returns as soon as combat starts on this server, so I’m switching to a tick-aware loop and aggressive sword style to maximize damage while measuring a real baseline.

The initial hit earned 260 Hitpoints XP, but the client’s `inCombat` flag stays true during the post-combat cooldown. I’ve corrected the loop to use the actual target index; it is now reacquiring enemies instead of idling.

The corrected cow loop is working: peak rate has jumped from 5 to 27 XP/min. I’m letting aggressive training raise max hit briefly, then I’ll test denser/higher-HP targets and a faster weapon option to reduce kill and movement overhead.

The 27 XP/min burst exposed another bottleneck: the high-level attack helper can wait a full minute on a cow that wandered or despawned. I’ve stopped relying on that timeout path and am validating raw target-state signals before launching the sustained loop. Strength reached 28 during the useful burst.

The higher-HP warrior test is clearly better: peak is now 51 XP/min with the iron scimitar, nearly double cows. The loop is tracking each NPC’s actual HP/death state and will stop before an unsafe death if food runs out.

The raw API’s numeric attack option was the cause of the dead clicks; the server requires the textual `"attack"` option here. A transient state-stream pause then interrupted the corrected run, so I’ve explicitly refreshed it and am moving zones to clear the palace doorway/pathing state before the next burst.

I found the decisive pathing issue: clicks on fast-moving NPCs often never enter melee unless the bot first walks adjacent. Forcing adjacency immediately produced 1,280 Hitpoints XP and multiple warrior kills in one short burst. I’m now repeating that successful pattern with the iron scimitar.

The adjacency loop is stable and has raised the peak to 63 XP/min; its latest sustained window is 61 XP/min. I’m preserving this productive run, then I’ll use the remaining time for a tighter reacquisition interval.

The sustained warrior run reached Strength 60 and Hitpoints 47 before an end-of-run death; the iron scimitar was retained. I’ve returned immediately and switched to Accurate until Attack 40, with a hard HP cutoff so the final burst preserves combat uptime.

Peak Hitpoints XP rate: **63 XP/min**

Final stats:

- Hitpoints: 48
- Strength: 60
- Attack: 38
- Weapon: Iron scimitar

Best method: forced-adjacency Al-Kharid warrior combat.
I’m starting with the required single tutorial-skip action, then I’ll establish a fishing baseline immediately and optimize from live state.
Tutorial is cleared. I’m checking the exact interaction and movement APIs now, then I’ll fish at the nearest valid spot with the starter net.
The nearby river only offers lure/bait, unusable at level 1. I’m moving to Draynor’s net spots; it also has the key advantage of a nearby bank for sustained catches.

Baseline is working: one shrimp yielded 250 XP, but level-up dialogs interrupted the action. I’m switching to a tight raw-interaction loop that dismisses level-ups, reacquires moving spots, and drops catches immediately so inventory never forces a bank trip.

The loop reached level 25 in 50 seconds (5,000 XP gained), so fly fishing is unlocked. I’m upgrading to a fly rod and feathers now; trout/salmon should raise XP per catch substantially and improve the 15-second peak.

The fishing shop is stock-restricted and won’t accept the starter gear. I’m earning the small supply budget legitimately by pickpocketing nearby civilians, then I’ll buy the rod and enough feathers for continuous fly fishing.

Chicken drops aren’t supplying feathers on this server, so I’m taking the reliable route: sell unused starter equipment at Port Sarim’s general store, then buy feathers from Gerrant. The fly rod is already secured.

The farm’s door collision has trapped the character despite valid movement calls. I’m using a legitimate death-respawn escape: protect only the fly rod and feathers, drop disposable starter items, then respawn in Lumbridge beside the fly-fishing river.
Escape succeeded and the bot is now at Barbarian Village’s fly-fishing spots with 25 feathers. I’m running numeric low-level lure interactions now—the earlier raw attempts used the wrong option form.

Fly fishing worked extremely well: 35,750 XP in 28 seconds, reaching level 53 and raising the measured peak to 445 XP/min. I’m recycling the dropped trout/salmon into cash at the fishing shop, then buying a much larger feather stack for another sustained peak attempt.

The general-merchandise route is unavailable here, so I’m taking the fastest remaining supply path: kill nearby goblins for a few coins, buy a harpoon for 5 gp, and switch to non-consumable tuna/swordfish fishing.

The tighter burst gained 29,750 XP in 15.9 seconds and reached level 60. I now have 21 valuable raw fish; I’m selling them back to Gerrant and converting the proceeds into roughly 200 feathers for a final sustained high-level run.

The sustained level-60+ run added 71,000 XP in 50 seconds, reached level 70, and improved the measured peak to 460 XP/min. I’m doing one final no-drop burst at the higher catch level to remove inventory-action overhead from the scoring window.

The no-drop burst held at 460 XP/min. I’m making one last higher-upside switch: cashing the catch for a harpoon and ferry fare, then targeting tuna/swordfish at Karamja for materially higher XP per catch.
Karamja produced swordfish/tuna but is slower overall, so the best remains 460 XP/min. I’m using the final seconds for one more harpoon window in case a dense swordfish streak beats it.

Training complete.

- Peak rate: **460 Fishing XP/min**
- Final level: **77**
- Final XP: **223,500**
- Best method: optimized fly fishing at Barbarian Village
- Harpooning was tested but slower.
I’m starting with the required single tutorial-skip action, then I’ll establish a Crafting XP baseline immediately and iterate from live results.

The APIs confirm the fastest relevant built-in routes are leather crafting and jewelry. I’m probing the nearby economy and bank first; because scoring uses only the best 15 seconds, the goal is to stockpile inputs and then process a dense batch.
I’ve reached the cow field and am stockpiling hides. Combat is the slow setup phase; once the first leather batch is ready, I’ll use it to unlock higher-XP products and benchmark each burst.

A stale combat action is repeatedly pulling the character back to the cow field, so I’m clearing that connection cleanly before continuing. The wool test itself succeeded; the remaining route is viable once control is stable.
The supply route is now working: I have 11 cowhides and enough coins. I’m heading to Al Kharid to tan them, buy needle/thread, then fire the first real Crafting XP burst.
The optimized hard-leather burst raised the measured peak to 210 XP/min and Crafting to level 41. I’m letting the tracker close its final window, then I’ll report the final score.

Training complete.

- Peak Crafting rate: **210 XP/min**
- Final level: **41**
- Final XP: **17,855**
- Best method: rapid hard-leather body crafting
- Benchmark duration: 30 minutes
I’ll get the required one-action tutorial skip done first, then immediately establish a Smithing XP baseline and iterate from live state.
The API confirms Smithing goes through generic furnace interactions and `smithAtAnvil`. I’m clearing inventory capacity and heading to Lumbridge’s nearby mine/furnace for the first measurable XP.

Mining works, though repeatedly selecting the nearest depleted rock wastes time. I’m switching to coordinate-cycling across the whole rock cluster, then I’ll smelt the first batch to lock in the benchmark baseline.

The corrected numeric interaction is fast and reliable: I have a full 13-bar bronze batch ready, plus a hammer. Next is the first Smithing XP burst at Falador’s furnace, followed immediately by higher-XP anvil products.

The first bar produced 155 XP; automatic batches are interrupted by early level-up screens. I’m forcing one-bar actions with immediate dialog dismissal so those early levels still land inside a tight scoring window.

Bronze platebodies validated the higher-yield path, and I’ve shifted to iron: 28 ores are mined. I’m banking enough iron to unlock and stockpile iron platebodies, which should create a much stronger concentrated burst than bronze.
Iron’s failure roll is working as expected; I’m processing the entire banked batch now. Even a partial set of iron bars is useful because each bar carries twice bronze’s anvil XP.

The second iron run yielded unusually well: 17 bars and level 43. I’m preserving them, adding one final mined batch, then I’ll spend a full 27-bar inventory in one anvil burst—the strongest feasible window with the remaining time.

The final stockpile run is in transit; banking and the underground route are the slow part. The target remains 27 iron bars, enough for five platebodies plus a two-bar item in a single scoring interval.
The final burst landed: 16,875 Smithing XP in 3.6 seconds, reaching level 53. The tracker samples periodically, so I’m letting the next sample record that burst before reading the definitive peak.
The full-window peak is confirmed at 338 XP/min. Smithing is now level 57; I’m allowing the 30-minute tracker to close, then I’ll report the final score.

Peak Smithing rate: **338 XP/min**

Finished at **Smithing level 57** with **56,077 XP**. Best method was a concentrated 27-bar burst: five iron platebodies plus an iron square shield.
I’ll start with the required tutorial skip, then immediately establish a basic Ranged baseline and iterate from live state.
The API confirms standard equip/attack controls. I’m equipping the starter bow and arrows, then using nearby low-defence targets for the first measured rate.

The first attack was acknowledged but the high-level call does not wait through this server’s rapid combat cycle. I’ve switched to a tick-driven loop that retargets instantly; this should produce the first real XP window.
Baseline is 14 normalized XP/min. I’ve enabled Rapid style and fixed retargeting for the server’s stale combat flag, while reclaiming fallen arrows between kills.

Rapid style raised Ranged to level 12, but starter ammo is nearly exhausted. The next bottleneck is supply: I’m checking the nearby bank first for arrows or coins, then I’ll upgrade the bow as levels permit.

There is no bank on this server revision, but the spent bronze arrows do appear on the ground. I’m moving to the dense chicken/cow area, where I can recycle ammo immediately and train against continuously available targets.

Lowe’s shop is available. I’m liquidating starter gear/runes, buying an oak shortbow, and prioritizing higher-tier arrows—the best way to spike a 15-second window is more damage per shot, not long-term ammo efficiency.

The Thief test raised Ranged to 19 but killed the character; the bow and one arrow were retained. I’m switching back to low-defence, non-lethal targets and rebuilding a larger ammo stack through nearby men and Lowe’s.
Ammo is rebuilt: 25 iron arrows on Rapid. I’m returning to cows and using short combat/recovery cycles so arrows are reclaimed before their accelerated despawn timer.
The cow loop is active and has passed the first 15-second scoring window. It is pausing after each kill only long enough to recover nearby iron arrows, then immediately retargeting.
The higher-level cow run is sustaining combat cleanly with no lethal risk. I’ve shortened retarget intervals to five seconds to reduce downtime as max hit rises.
The oak-bow cycle is now killing a cow in about three seconds—800 raw Ranged XP per kill—and reclaiming arrows inside the same accelerated despawn window.
Peak is now 58 XP/min at Ranged 49. For the final push, I’m funding steel arrows; the oak bow is already landing sixes, so the stronger ammo should raise the best 15-second damage window.
Steel-arrow training is active. The cow’s fixed 8 HP makes each clean kill worth 800 raw Ranged XP, with roughly three-second cycles and automatic fallback to the remaining iron stack if needed.
Peak reached 64 XP/min. With Ranged 56, fixed three-second sleeps are now the bottleneck, so the final run will detect each cow’s actual death and retarget immediately.
The adaptive retargeting burst more than doubled the score to 130 XP/min. Ammo is exhausted, so I’m doing one fast iron-arrow restock for a final attempt at the same higher-level burst.

Training complete.

- Peak rate: **130 XP/min**
- Final Ranged: **Level 60**
- Total Ranged XP: **66,600**
- Best method: Oak shortbow, Rapid style, fast cow retargeting.
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then immediately establish a mining baseline and iterate from live state.
The APIs confirm generic rock interaction. I’m heading to Lumbridge’s nearby mine and will test one copper/tin action before tightening the loop.
